description: Designing an interactive space mission game that'll keep you on the edge of your seats and also excited to play it
summary:
Earth: The Beginning. You walk the launch pad, inspect stations, and fill out a pre-launch checklist. You balance fuel load (the rocket equation, where too little fuel stalls the climb and too much adds dead weight), oxygen reserves, battery power, and launch angle.
Orbit: The Unknown. You fly the ship toward the Moon, dodging debris and collecting solar orbs.
Moon: The Silent Frontier. As an astronaut on the surface, you scan crater anomalies to find water ice and set up solar power and a rover.
Space Station: Signal Lost. You restore communications by tuning frequency and phase on an oscilloscope until the signal locks. You also repair three relay systems and survive a solar storm by managing radiation shielding.
Rescue Operation. You drive the rover across the lunar terrain, following beacons to rescue three astronauts while watching slope, traction and power draw.
The return. The crew escapes, the shuttle rendezvous with lunar orbit, and the capsule re-enters and parachutes down to a splashdown. The game ends on “The End.”
details:
A Space rescue mission which based on Moon. The story follows a space research team heading to moon but meet an unseen accident and are trapped on moon. The player is the rescuer astronaut who flies to moon, locates their debris. Retrieves the blackbox and decodes its last radio signals to find their last known positions on Moon. Then uses the rover to rescue them.

We've used Three.js and WebGL to run the game on the browser so that it can be run on any computer.

You need use a google account to play the games since it was developed in Google AI Studio.
